ascii-transaction.title: ASCII poll of the data frame
ascii-transaction.alt: One ASCII poll of a BASIS 2: the host sends the unit ID and a carriage return, the line stays idle for the serial idle timeout, and the instrument answers with one line of the data frame ended by a carriage return.
ascii-transaction.description: The TX lane is what the host sends and the RX lane what the instrument answers, left to right in time. On TX the unit ID A and a carriage return poll the whole data frame; after the idle timeout the instrument sends on RX its unit ID, the temperature, flow and the other fields (some are left out) and the gas, then a carriage return. The table gives the idle timeout in byte times.

chip-blocks.title: Inside the BASIS 2
chip-blocks.alt: Block diagram of the BASIS 2: its function blocks, how they connect and which package pins reach each block.
chip-blocks.description: The BASIS 2's function blocks inside its outline. Arrows between blocks carry signals or data in the direction they point (both ways where they have two heads). The package pins stand on the left and right edges with their numbers, each wired to the block it reaches.

chip-capabilities.title: What the BASIS 2 does
chip-capabilities.alt: Capability map of the BASIS 2: Flow, temperature and total (supported): Polls the whole data frame or single items and decodes each number exactly; Setpoint, ramp and watchdog (supported): Sets the flow of a controller, limits how fast it changes and closes the valve if the line goes quiet; Valve hold and loop gains (supported): Holds the valve at a fixed drive, opens or closes it, and tunes the closed loop; Tare and autotare (supported): Zeroes the flow reading at no flow, and on a controller zeroes it again at a closed setpoint; Gas selection (supported): Selects one of the nine calibrated gases and lists the gases the instrument holds; Totalizer and batch (supported): Counts the gas that has passed, sets what happens at the limit, and dispenses a set volume; Measurement window (supported): Starts a timed measurement, by command or by an event, and reads its averages and ranges; Unit ID, baud and protocol (guarded): Changes the unit ID, address, baud rate or protocol, restores factory settings, and scans a line; Analog setpoint and output (not covered): A 0 to 5 V or 4 to 20 mA setpoint input and flow output on pins 1 and 2, wired outside the driver.
chip-capabilities.description: Each card is one function of the BASIS 2: an icon, its name and what it does for the application. The filled pill says how this driver covers it (legend below); the outlined pills are the chip registers behind it. The coverage table in the README gives the driver calls and the datasheet section of each card.

chip-circuit-rs232.title: BASIS 2: RS-232 point to point
chip-circuit-rs232.alt: Schematic of the BASIS 2 rs-232 point to point: the chip with U2 MCU, U3 RS-232 level shifter, J1 12 to 24 V supply; the MCU wires carry the port hooks Read(), Write().
chip-circuit-rs232.description: A schematic. The MCU is on the left, each of its pins level with the chip pin it connects to; above each wire is the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it. Supply pins point up to their supply and decoupling, ground pins down. Pins on the right carry the loads and the pins tied to a supply or ground; a cross marks a pin left open. A dot is a junction; wires that cross without a dot are not connected.

chip-hero.title: BASIS 2
chip-hero.alt: Overview of the BASIS 2, a family of gas mass flow meters (B series) and controllers (BC series): it reports the flow, temperature and total of nine gases, and a controller sets the flow with its own valve. A MCU talks to it over RS-232 or RS-485; it drives Valve; it reads back Gas flow, Gas temperature. Headline figures: 12 to 24 V supply on pin 4 only; 1000:1 turndown, 0.1 to 100 % of full scale; 9 gases selectable, stored in the instrument; 176 Hz digital update rate at best.
chip-hero.description: The BASIS 2 in the middle, drawn as its JST GH 6-pin connector package. On the left the MCU that runs the driver, joined to it by RS-232 or RS-485. To the right, what the chip drives, in the order the power flows. Below it, what the chip reads back. The tiles at the bottom are the headline numbers, each with the datasheet section and page it comes from.

chip-outline.alt: Outline of the BASIS 2 in JST GH 6-pin connector drawn to scale from above: body 68.6 x 22.2 x 39.4 mm, 6 pins.

chip-pinout.title: BASIS 2 pinout, JST GH 6-pin connector
chip-pinout.alt: Pinout of the BASIS 2 in JST GH 6-pin connector, top view: 6 pins, each with its name, its electrical type as a colour and the driver hook that uses it.
chip-pinout.description: The BASIS 2 seen from the top, in its JST GH 6-pin connector package. Pin 1 is marked by the dot; the numbers run counter-clockwise from it. Each pad is coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). driver-layers.title: The layers, one of them yours
driver-layers.alt: Layer diagram: your application calls the Basis2 core, which sends register reads and writes through the UART port contract to the port class you write, which drives the chip; the core and the contract are the same on every MCU.
driver-layers.description: Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers.

one-call-through-the-layers.title: One call through the layers
one-call-through-the-layers.alt: One ReadFlow call: the device class builds the request, the bus layer waits for silence, writes it through your port and reads until a carriage return, and the reply is checked and decoded into a flow value.
one-call-through-the-layers.description: Participants, left to right: Your code, Basis2, Bus and Your port. The steps run from top to bottom. Your code sends ReadFlow() to Basis2. Basis2 does ascii::Make(Poll) builds and checks the bytes itself. Basis2 sends Execute(request, timing) to Bus. A note over Bus says: wait t3.5 of silence. Bus sends FlushInput(), Write("A\r") to Your port. A note over Bus and Your port says: Repeat until a CR or the deadline. Bus sends Read(buffer) to Your port. A note over Bus and Your port says: End of the repeated steps. Your port returns "A +012.30 +024.8 ... Air\r" to Bus. Bus returns Reply to Basis2. A note over Basis2 says: strict grammar, unit ID, range. Basis2 returns Result of Decimal to Your code.

rs485-topology.title: Several BASIS 2 on one RS-485 line
rs485-topology.alt: An RS-485 line on which an MCU and up to 26 BASIS 2 instruments share the B (+) and A (-) wires, each answering to its own unit ID in ASCII or its own Modbus address in Modbus RTU.
rs485-topology.description: The MCU on top and the BASIS 2 instruments under it connect to the rails B (+) and A (-) on the right, on pins 5 and 6 of each connector; the dashed card stands for the instruments in between. Each instrument needs a unique unit ID, A to Z, for ASCII and a unique Modbus address, 1 to 247, for Modbus RTU.

uart-timing.title: UART character
uart-timing.alt: One serial character of the BASIS 2 at its factory settings: a start bit, eight data bits least significant first and one stop bit with no parity, at 38400 bit/s unless the baud rate was changed.
uart-timing.description: The lane is TX, left to right in time, and the RX line carries the same format in the other direction. The line idles high, the start bit pulls it low for one bit time, the data bits D0 to D7 follow and the stop bit returns it high. The table gives the default bit rate and the range of rates the instrument can be set to.
